chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, who said:

Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Imran al-Hamdani wrote to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): 'I performed Hajj, and I am an adversary (of the Hajj rites), and I was a novice (first-timer), so I entered performing Tamattu' (Umrah followed by Hajj).' He (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'Repeat your Hajj.'

key_terms.صَرُورَةً: A novice or first-timer (one who has not performed Hajj before)
key_terms.مُتَمَتِّعاً: Performing Tamattu' (combining Umrah and Hajj with a break in between)
key_terms.مُخَالِفٌ: One who is not compliant or proficient in the rites

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a first-time pilgrim who is not proficient in Hajj rituals?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Hamdani writes to Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) regarding his Hajj, noting he was a novice ('mukhālif') and inexperienced ('ṣarūrah') when performing the Tamattu' rite. The Imam’s directive to repeat the Hajj underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on the necessity of competence and proper execution of rituals, particularly for those new to the practice, to ensure the validity of the obligation.
